intro: How to say what hurts, whether you have a fever, and where there is a pharmacy.
p.me duele.glosa: one part of my body hurts
p.me duele.consejo: Duele goes with one thing: «me duele la cabeza». The thing that hurts is the subject.
p.me duelen.glosa: several parts of my body hurt
p.me duelen.consejo: With two or more things you say «me duelen los ojos», «me duelen las piernas».
p.la cabeza.glosa: the part of the body above the neck
p.la cabeza.consejo: With body parts you do not say «mi»: you say «me duele la cabeza».
p.los ojos.glosa: the part of the body we see with
p.los ojos.consejo: The j sounds like a strong h: «O-hos». You say «me duelen los ojos».
p.el estómago.glosa: the part of the body where food goes
p.el estómago.consejo: The accent mark shows the strong syllable: es-TO-ma-go. You say «me duele el estómago».
p.fiebre.consejo: With fiebre we use «tener»: «tengo fiebre». You do not say «me duele la fiebre».
p.la farmacia.consejo: In Spain c before i sounds like «th»: «far-MA-thya».
p.cerca.consejo: Alone it works: «hay una farmacia cerca». With a place it takes de: «cerca de casa».
b1.texto:
To say what hurts use **doler**. The thing that hurts is the **subject** and it usually comes after the verb:

- One thing: **me duele** → **Me duele la cabeza.**
- Several things: **me duelen** → **Me duelen los ojos.**

For a fever you do not use doler: you use **tener** → **Tengo fiebre.** And to ask: **¿Tienes fiebre?**

If you need medicine, ask for a **farmacia** and say it is **cerca**: **Hay una farmacia cerca.**
b2.f2.texto: I do not have a fever.
b2.f7.texto: Let us go to the pharmacy.
b4.titulo: Doler: the thing that hurts is the subject
b4.texto:
The verb **doler** works like **gustar**:

- It goes with a person: **me, te, le, nos, os, les**.
- It is **singular** if one thing hurts: **me duele el estómago**.
- It is **plural** if several things hurt: **me duelen los ojos**.

The verb agrees with the thing that hurts, not with the person. Before the body part use **el, la, los, las**, not «mi».

A **fever** does not hurt: you have it → **tengo fiebre**.
b5.f0.texto: A grey light comes in through the bedroom window.
b5.f1.texto: A dull thud beats inside Lucía's head.
b5.f2.texto: Her eyes hurt like two small embers.
b5.f3.texto: Her stomach rests under the soft blanket.
b5.f4.texto: A cold thermometer waits on the bedside table.
b5.f5.texto: Lucía walks slowly down the cool morning street.
b5.f6.texto: The pharmacy is nearby and shines with a green cross.
b5.f7.texto: A little bell rings above the glass door.
b5.f8.texto: A clean smell of herbs fills the fresh air.
b5.f9.texto: The pharmacist smiles and hands her a small box.
b6.o0.refuerzo: That's it! One single thing hurts: «duele».
b6.o1.refuerzo: «Duelen» is plural, but the head is just one.
b6.o2.refuerzo: «Me» is missing: it says who is in pain.
b6.pregunta: You want to say your head hurts. What do you say?
b7.o0.refuerzo: Yes: the eyes are several, so it goes in the plural.
b7.o1.refuerzo: «Duele» is for one single thing; here there are two eyes.
b7.o2.refuerzo: «Dolor» is a noun, not a verb. A verb is missing here.
b7.pregunta: Which verb form goes with «los ojos»?
b8.traduccion: There is a pharmacy very close
b9.o0.refuerzo: A fever does not hurt: you have it.
b9.o1.refuerzo: Well done! With fiebre you use «tener».
b9.o2.refuerzo: «Estar» does not go with fiebre: you say «tienes fiebre».
b9.pregunta: You want to know if someone has a fever. What do you ask?
b10.o0.refuerzo: A pharmacy is a place, not a body part.
b10.o1.refuerzo: A fever does not hurt: you say «tengo fiebre».
b10.o2.refuerzo: Correct: it is a body part and it is masculine.
b12.o0.refuerzo: The head is a body part, not a place to go.
b12.o1.refuerzo: A fever is a symptom, not a place.
b12.o2.refuerzo: Yes! They sell medicine at the pharmacy.
b12.pregunta: You feel ill and need medicine. Where do you go?
p.duelen.consejo: Plural of «duele»: «duelen». Use it when several things hurt: «me duelen los ojos». The «ue» is one syllable.
p.sordo.consejo: Stress on the first syllable: «SOR-do». It also means someone who cannot hear: «una persona sorda».
p.late.consejo: From «latir», said of the heart or of a throbbing pain. Stress on the first syllable: «LA-te».
p.brasas.consejo: The s sounds like s, not z: «BRA-sas». Singular: «una brasa». Eyes that sting «like embers».
p.manta.consejo: Stress on the first syllable: «MAN-ta». Feminine: «la manta». Not to be confused with «mano», the hand.
p.termómetro.consejo: The accent falls on the third-to-last syllable: «ter-MO-me-tro». Masculine, like almost all words ending in -o.
p.mesita.consejo: «Mesa» + -ita = a little table: «me-SI-ta». «Mesita de noche» is the bedside table.
p.cruz.consejo: One syllable, and the final z sounds «th»: «KRUTH». The plural changes z to c: «cruces».
p.campanita.consejo: «Campana» + -ita = a little bell: «kam-pa-NI-ta». The ending -ita makes things small and cute.
p.limpio.consejo: «io» is one syllable: «LIM-pyo». The opposite is «sucio». Feminine: «limpia».
p.hierbas.consejo: The h is silent and «ie» is one syllable: «YER-bas». It comes from «hierba», feminine.
p.farmacéutico.consejo: The accent mark falls on the third-to-last syllable: «far-ma-THEU-ti-ko». The c before e sounds «th».
p.entrega.consejo: From «entregar», to hand something to someone. The g is hard, as in «go»: «en-TRE-ga».
p.estómago.consejo: The accent mark shows the stress on «TO»: «es-TO-ma-go». Masculine: «el estómago». «Me duele el estómago».
